 my mom continued to decline over the next few days and despite our continued verbal concern to physicians and nurses it seemed to fall on deaf ears.  on 5/2 i spoke with the evening jacqueline m. and who told us on her icu admission he felt he could pull her through this.  we were very present in the icu only leaving at bedtime and back in the am.  our only mistake was asking kris keough the ethicist not to be involved in my mother's care. we only saw dr. yen on her icu admission and never came back at all during her admission to speak with my sister or myself, we were both her poa's. on friday may 3rd physician rounding was taking place and visitors are asked to leave.  kris keoug went into my mother's room and told her she was dying.  she told this to my mother alone with no support person in the room.  not only doing this to my mom there was never a family conference to discuss my mom's care or she may not survive this hospitalization.  kris came to the waiting room, blindsided dr. kosari is a terrible, careless, incompetent surgeon. do not trust him. i've made that mistake twice, so i'm not sure which of us is the bigger idiot. i've tried to summarize my experience with him below, but happy to describe in more detail through message for those considering a surgery with dr. kosari.

in 2013, i started to develop an umbilical hernia just above my belly button. it was never that noticeable, but in the spring of 2019, it had grown just enough to always be noticeable to me. i was referred to dr. kosari. i thought that the reputation of cedars-sinai would hold, but i was wrong.

in the examination, dr. kosari was friendly, but clearly rushed. he let me know he only had about 10 minutes. i explained i'd had the hernia for a few years and, while seated, he asked me to lift my shirt, briefly touched the belly button (literally for less than a second) where it was visible and that was it for the exam. he said he'd recommend doing the surgery with stitches, not mesh. knowing nothing about the difference, i trusted his judgment.

the day of the surgery, i was a bit tense as this was my first surgery. i was also concerned he had not adequately inspected the hernia (and he had not ordered any type of ultrasound). i waited for about 2 hours and then they took me in to prepare me. when i saw dr. kosari before the surgery, i explicitly asked him, "so you are going to be able to fix not only the part below the belly button, but also above it, right?" dr. kosari responded, "yes, don't worry. once we're in, we'll be able to check it all to see what we're dealing with."

i woke up after the procedure and went home. i had the surgery on friday, sep 13. i removed the bandage (which was covering the belly button and surrounding area) and showered on sunday, sep 15. by monday, i felt the hernia above my belly button exactly as before the surgery. panic immediately struck. i called cedars-sinai and was able to tell dr. kosari's nurse i felt a bulge exactly like the hernia, and she told me to just come in for my checkup in 2 weeks for dr. kosari to examine it.

when dr. kosari examined me, he tried to say there was nothing wrong, or that it was something else (like a result from the surgery or a problem with "skin" being "detached"). i told him, "no...i am 100% sure this is the same hernia i've had...it feels exactly the same." he told me to come back in 4 more weeks after the recovery period "to see if it's still there." that really aggravated me, i left the appointment knowing i still had the hernia, but he wouldn't acknowledge it.

at the next appointment, he acknowledged i still had a hernia, but never acknowledged it was because of his carelessness. compared to the first surgery, he was pushing much more strongly for not operating again. i think it's because it would make him look bad to have to repeat the exact same surgery, but i scheduled a follow up surgery for dec 3 anyway to get it dealt with once and for all (had already pretty much met my out of pocket max, so thought why not - and couldn't get in to ucla before the end of the calendar year - book ahead!).

on dec 3, i had the second surgery, and this time we did an ultrasound before the surgery. again, he did not recommend mesh, just a single stitch he said. this time, i didn't notice the hernia for a few weeks, but could definitely feel a slight bump, which i thought might be the stitch or something. now, just over 6 weeks since the second surgery, i still have the hernia. i can feel it exactly the same as i used to.

after one surgery, i'd expect a hernia to be fixed, at least for a few years before it might recur. after two surgeries, i would really expect a hernia to be fixed. now, after spending thousands of dollars, taking months off from the gym for two separate recoveries, and still having the problem that was supposed to be fixed, i'm so filled with anger and frustration about this "doctor." he is careless, negligent, or uses poor judgment in making choices for his patients' care. 

please, do not select this doctor. i will be seeing dr. chen from ucla instead....happy to compare my experience after my third hernia surgery for the same hernia. in my last check-up after the second surgery, dr. kosari told me, "if it comes back let me know and we can go back in there with the mesh." to myself, i thought this moron will never touch my body again. don't let yourself become another one of his mistakes. i will forever regret it, but hopefully i can get a successful surgery from ucla and eventually put this behind me. but i'm sure i will continue to live with the nightmares about the hernia problems that i've had ever since the first surgery was unsuccessful, i hope you can learn from my pain and experience to avoid the same experience with this terrible doctor. cedars-sinai should not allow this man to be operating under their name.

as they say, "fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice shame on me." he won't be fooling me a third time.

let's start with the g6 sensors themselves and the fact that since october 2018, the average amount of time a sensor lasts on my son is a paltry 4.33 days (only 8 sensors since then have lasted the full 10 days!)i've tried everything to get them to last longer, from listening to all the (often contradictory) advice that support reps give - one person tells me to pinch the skin at the attachment site before attaching, another person tells me not to do that. we've tried hydrating him more, that didn't work. someone even told us to try not to calibrate if we can avoid it, because that throws the sensor into a tailspin and eventually it will fail. more on what a messy situation that is later. what i had been doing about all these sensor failures up until a few months ago, was when i got a chance, i would call in with the information i captured in a spreadsheet (lot #, attachment date, attachment location on the body, whether or not i applied an overpatch, the date it was removed and the reason for removal) and the support specialist would take the total number of days i should have gotten out of x sensors, subtract out the number of days i did get, and round up to the next number of sensors, and 3-5 days later, i'd have the sensors replaced. for instance, if 7 sensors lasted 34 days, the support rep would say "7 sensors should last 70 days. they lasted 34, so we owe you 36 days, which you can get out of 36/10 = 3.6 or 4 sensors." it wasn't ideal, but as a very busy person, being able to call in when i could to get sensors replaced was the only thing that made all these sensor failures halfway tolerable.

then, they instituted a policy that they would replace only 3 sensors per call, and the rest would have to be approved, adding a new dimension to the dysfunction that is the g6. customer support reps continually assure me that i am not the only one having these issues, so why in the hell would they institute a policy like this when there are so many problems with the g6? now instead of waiting to do this when i can, i have to call every time one fails? i just don't have the time to do that! the same person who first apprised me of this policy  told me i could send email instead of calling. great! but then i get a return email asking me to take more time i don't have to fill out a patient request form (the description field of which accepts 126 characters max!), and then after i've done that, now i have to wait an additional 2-3 business days to get a call back, and even if that happens on time (which it doesn't always) over the course of all of this, 2 more sensors have failed. they've created a bottleneck with this 3-sensor-limit policy. most of the time, they approve the 3 sensors and leave any remaining sensors in limbo waiting for "approval."  i had needed 6 sensors, the rep who i was on the phone with sent 3, and told me i'd have to wait for the other 3 to be approved. after not hearing back for about 3 weeks, i called in and the rep just sent the sensors. so what was the fucking point of that? they didn't even need to get approved! they just added a layer to make it more difficult for me. i patronize the company because it is supposed to provide working devices, and when they don't work, to have them replaced swiftly, not to create impediments for every type of problem i could have and then not even stick to those policies. dexcom should be creating solutions, not problems.

finally, dexcom g6 has this habit of asking me to recalibrate every 15 minutes if the fingerstick calibration value is too far off from the sensor reading. on christmas night at about 11:35pm the sensor reported my son's bg was low, and before i go throwing glucose down his throat, i did a fingerstick. the fingerstick came back with 93, and when i calibrated, it told me to recalibrate after 11:50pm. it's almost midnight and i'd really like to go to sleep, but i figured i'd play along. at about midnight, i fingerstick again,106. i put that in the dexcom app. now it wants me to calibrate after 12:05am." so then i do it again, and it says calibrate at 12:20m.  i don't have time to jerk this thing off.  dexcom openly admits it is for information purposes and may not be accurate and also admit that the fingerstick is the more accurate indicator of what the blood sugar actually is. then why on earth do i have to keep doing this for hours even at 1 in the morning when i want to sleep because the fingerstick doesn't agree with dexcom!? when i put in the fingerstick value it should adjust to that, period. this calibrate over and over again is pure horseshit and it goes against everything we know about which is the accurate one and which is to be used for information purposes! now support would say "after the 2nd or 3rd calibration, you should just replace the sensor." but you can see why i want every sensor to last as long as possible, because every sensor failure is is another addition to the boondoggle that is the sensor replacement process.

doc_text:
during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

once in the er, which was set up efficiently because of the virus, the er doctor immediately explained to me that they will not send my covid-19 test off to be tested unless i was admitted to the hospital.  his main concern was not diagnosing my problem but explaining that i would have to go somewhere else to get tested for covid-19.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.  

i was discharged and walked to my car still struggling to breath just the same way as i walked into the hospital.   

that was saturday, march 21st. fast forward to wednesday, march 25th and i was not feeling any better, in fact, i felt worse. i called my doctor both the 25th and 26th and left messages. her nurse called my back on the 27th and informed me to stop taking all allergy meds immediately and that she had reviewed the labs and x-rays and they believe that haze over my right lung is pneumonia.

pneumonia?!!  so i had pneumonia in the right lung for an additional 6 days without any treatment?!  why would dr. parker say i was "all clear" and ignore the haze?  i had to take additional time from work to heal whereas if dr. parker would have just taken the time to explore my results for something more than covid-19, he could have treated me correctly and i could have returned back to work without taking additional time.  

lastly, once i got the bill, i saw that i was billed $273.50 for a pregnancy test!!!  the admitting nurse asked if there was anyway i could be pregnant, i immediately answered no and explained why i couldn't be.  so why would you give me, a 49 yr old woman with a valid reason a pregnancy test?  especially for $273.50.  over billing???   yes!

i will never go back to memorial hermann sugar land emergency room.  the care of the treating physician was below sub-par and i could have saved way more time and money going to another facility.

doc_text: pch  is a great hospital with world class providers. the billing dept, however, is another story. the billing dept at pch represents what is wrong with american healthcare.  my daughter was seen by an ophthamologist in the pch network in 2018. the visit was covered by our insurance minus our usual co-pay.  in 2019, we made another appointment to visit the same ophthamologist and again, paid our usual co-pay at the time of the visit. one year later, we received a bill for the visit from phoenix children's for $418.  it appears that the visit was coded as a routine eye exam which is not covered under the medical benefit of my insurance. i submitted the claim to my eye insurance and received reimbursement of $45. if insurance had covered this appointment, it would have paid a contracted rate that was significantly lower than $418.  i called the number on the bill and the person told me that was the standard charge for the visit and that i could pay it, but otherwise, there was nothing more she could do.  i asked her for options and she did not seem to be very concerned with helping me.  she said that if i didn't want to pay the bill, that after 6 months, the account would be sent to collections and i could just pay them. i was appalled at the lack of concern or the willingness to help. why should i be saddled with a bill of $418 because i am a cash customer when my insurance would have paid a significantly lower rate. i am just looking to be treated fairly and pch should be ashamed for how they treat their patients and their families.

doc_text:
i went to centennial medical plaza on memorial day for abdominal pain that had left me unable to eat or drink anything for the previous three days.  i was vomiting and having terrible spasms. i was even crying from the pain.

we went to centennial medical plaza, where the nurses were great, especially lois.  very helpful and caring. but the doctor  seemed uncaring and unhelpful.

i am allergic to chemicals and antibiotics.  i wouldn't allow the contrast dye to be injected prior to the cat scan because it's very toxic.  i also wouldn't allow the antibiotics because i am allergic to so many of them.
i didn't want to die seeking help for my issues!

the dr.  seemed annoyed with me and wouldn't give me anything for pain, nausea or anything else.  i did receive two bags of iv fluids.  i was sent home with a script.  all of this took 3 hours.

the radiologist wrote on my permanent medical records form that "stranding in anterior abdominal wall, possibly related to subcutaneous injections".  the radiologist must think i'm a drug addict whose been injecting myself in my abdominal area.  this is all without ever examining my abdominal  skin which shows no sign of injections.  i had the md"s at uc health er verify that by actually examining me.  what a concept! 
what an insult!  i don't use illicit drugs.  i just wanted something for pain so i could stop crying, stop vomiting, maybe eat or drink something and to be more comfortable.  the pain wears me out and keeps me from having a life.

please don't ever, ever, ever go to this place.  haven't received a bill from there yet, so i can't address that.  

the next day i went to the er at uc medical center at anschutz center in aurora (the old fitzsimmons area).

excellent care received at their very busy er department.  they took care of the pain, nausea and even gave me prescriptions for follow up. they found a gastric ulcer by x-ray and gave me a script for a liquid medication that is actually helping.   i would recommend going there anytime a decent and competent er is needed.  i will never go back to centennial medical plaza for anything.
